headline: Burnham says Brexit has not worked as UK and EU prepare for Friday's Brussels summit

terms.meaning: An arrangement where countries charge the same taxes on goods coming from outside the group and trade freely inside it.
The EU area where goods, services, money and people can move without trade barriers.
A scheme that puts a price on pollution so firms pay for the carbon they release.

levels.headline: Burnham says Brexit has not worked as UK and EU prepare for Friday's Brussels summit
levels.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said in a Lord Mayor's Banquet speech in London on Monday that Brexit has not delivered and that Britain needs a much closer relationship with the European Union. He spoke ahead of a UK-EU summit in Brussels on Friday 20 November.
The summit is expected to seal a trade deal covering food and drink, agreements on energy and emissions trading, and a scheme letting young people work for limited periods across Britain and the EU. Mr Burnham is due to meet European Council President Antonio Costa and Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. He said he will open a national conversation on the UK's long-term relationship with the bloc soon after the summit.
He remains bound by a pledge from his predecessor, Sir Keir Starmer, not to rejoin the customs union or single market before the next general election. Separately, the leaders of Belgium, Germany, Denmark, Luxembourg and the Netherlands wrote around 10 November asking that UK access to the EU electricity market depend on a financial contribution to EU regional funds. A later draft statement reportedly dropped the explicit wording, though a payment is still possible.
levels.why: The summit will shape UK trade, energy costs and young people's chances to work abroad.

levels.headline: Burnham: Brexit 'hasn't worked' as he heads to EU summit on Friday
levels.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham told a Lord Mayor's Banquet audience in London on Monday that Brexit has not worked and that the UK needs a much closer relationship with the EU. He was speaking before Friday's summit in Brussels.
That summit is expected to agree a food and drink trade deal, arrangements on energy and emissions trading, and a youth scheme allowing young people to work in the UK and EU for limited periods. Soon afterwards Mr Burnham says he will start a national conversation about Britain's long-term ties with the bloc.
The limits are clear. Sir Keir Starmer promised not to rejoin the customs union or single market before the next election, and Mr Burnham is bound by that. Five EU states, Belgium, Germany, Denmark, Luxembourg and the Netherlands, have also asked that British access to the electricity market come with a contribution to EU regional funds, though a later draft reportedly softened that wording.
levels.why: The deal could change what UK firms pay to trade and what households pay for energy.

levels.headline: Burnham says Brexit has failed to deliver ahead of crucial EU summit
levels.body:
Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister, used a speech in London on Monday to say that Brexit has not delivered and that Britain needs a much closer relationship with the European Union. A summit with EU leaders takes place in Brussels this Friday.
Officials expect it to produce a trade agreement on food and drink, deals on energy and emissions trading, and a plan for young people to work for limited periods in Britain and the EU. After the summit, Mr Burnham plans to begin a national conversation about the country's long-term relationship with the bloc.
There are constraints. Mr Burnham is bound by Sir Keir Starmer's pledge not to rejoin the customs union or single market before the next general election. Five EU countries have asked that the UK pay into regional development funds in return for electricity market access. A later draft of the summit text reportedly removed the explicit wording, but some payment may still be agreed.
levels.why: Whatever is agreed on Friday will affect trade, energy bills and travel for young people.

levels.headline: Burnham says Brexit has not worked, ahead of Friday's summit with the EU
levels.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Monday that Brexit has not delivered what was promised, and that the UK needs a much closer relationship with the European Union. He made the remarks in a speech in London before a summit in Brussels on Friday.
The summit is expected to bring a trade deal for food and drink, agreements on energy and the carbon market, and a scheme allowing young people to work in the UK and EU for limited periods. Mr Burnham says he will then open a national conversation about the UK's long-term relationship with the EU.
He remains tied to Sir Keir Starmer's promise not to rejoin the customs union or single market before the next election. Meanwhile five EU countries want Britain to contribute to EU regional funds in return for access to the electricity market. A later draft of the summit statement reportedly dropped that wording, but a payment has not been ruled out.
levels.why: It affects what we pay for food and energy, and whether young people can work abroad more easily.

levels.headline: Burnham says Brexit has not worked as he prepares for a big EU meeting
levels.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Monday that Brexit has not worked for Britain. He wants the UK to have a much closer relationship with the European Union, our nearest neighbours and biggest trading partner. On Friday he will go to Brussels to meet EU leaders.
At that meeting, the two sides are expected to agree a deal making it easier to trade food and drink. They should also agree things on energy and on pricing pollution, and a plan letting young people spend a limited time working in the UK or the EU. Mr Burnham then wants a national conversation about what kind of relationship the country wants in future.
There are limits. The government has promised not to rejoin the customs union, a shared system for taxing imports, or the single market before the next election. Five EU countries also want the UK to pay into EU funds in return for sharing electricity markets. The final wording may change.
levels.why: The agreement could make food cheaper to trade and give young people more chances abroad.

levels.headline: The Prime Minister says Brexit hasn't worked and wants closer ties with the EU
levels.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham says leaving the European Union has not worked out for Britain. In a speech in London on Monday, he said the UK should have a much closer relationship with the EU. On Friday he will meet EU leaders in Brussels.
Both sides are expected to sign deals on food and drink trade, on energy, and on a scheme to cut pollution by making firms pay for it. They also plan to let young people work for short periods in the UK and the EU. After that, Mr Burnham says he will start a national conversation about the long-term relationship, so the public can have a say.
He cannot go as far as some would like. His government has promised not to rejoin the customs union or the single market before the next general election. Five EU countries also say Britain should pay into EU funds if it wants to share the electricity market. Talks on that point are still going on.
levels.why: These deals could change prices in shops and give young people new chances to work abroad.

levels.headline: The PM says Brexit has not worked and meets EU leaders on Friday
levels.body:
The Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, says Brexit has not worked. He gave a speech in London on Monday. He said Britain should get much closer to the European Union, which is a group of 27 European countries that work together. On Friday he will go to Brussels to meet its leaders.
They are expected to agree to make trading food and drink easier. They may also agree to share some rules on energy and pollution. A third idea would let young people work in the UK or the EU for a short time. Mr Burnham says he will then ask the public what kind of long-term relationship they want.
There are limits. The government has promised not to rejoin the single market, which is the EU's big shared shop floor with no trade barriers. Five EU countries also want Britain to pay some money if it wants to use the shared electricity system. That part is still being talked about.
levels.why: It could change what things cost and where young people can work.

levels.headline: The Prime Minister wants Britain to be closer to Europe again
levels.body:
Britain left the European Union in 2020. This is called Brexit. Now the Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, says it has not worked well. On Monday he said Britain should get much closer to the EU. The EU is a group of European countries that trade and work together.
On Friday he will meet EU leaders in Brussels. They hope to agree some deals. One would make it easier to sell food and drink between Britain and the EU. Another is about energy. A third would let young people work in Britain or the EU for a short time. Mr Burnham also wants to ask people across the country what they think.
There are limits. Britain will not rejoin the EU's shared market before the next election. Some EU countries also want Britain to pay money if it uses their electricity system. Talks about this are still going on.
levels.why: The deals could change prices in shops and let young people work abroad.

levels.headline: The Prime Minister says leaving the EU has not worked well
levels.body:
Britain used to be part of a big group of countries called the European Union. We left a few years ago. The Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, now says leaving did not work well. He says Britain should be much closer friends with the group again.
On Friday he will go to a meeting in a city called Brussels. There he will meet the leaders of the group. They want to agree some new rules. One would make it easier to send food and drink between Britain and Europe. Another would let young people work in Britain or Europe for a short time.
The Prime Minister will not take Britain back into the group yet. He has promised that. But he wants to ask everyone in the country what they think. Some countries in the group also want Britain to pay some money for sharing electricity. That has not been decided.
levels.why: New rules could make food easier to trade and let young people work abroad.

levels.headline: Britain's leader wants to be friends with Europe again
levels.body:
Think of Europe as a big club of countries. Britain used to be in the club, then left. Now the Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, says leaving was not a good idea. He wants Britain to be much closer to the club again, like a friend who wants to play with the group.
On Friday he will visit the club's leaders in a city called Brussels. They hope to agree some new things. Food and drink could be sent between Britain and Europe more easily. Young people could go and work in Europe for a little while, and young people from Europe could work here.
Britain will not rejoin the club straight away. Some of the other countries also say Britain should chip in some money if it wants to share their electricity, a bit like paying to join in a game. Everyone is still talking about it.
levels.why: It could mean easier trips to work in Europe, and food that is easier to trade.

headline: S&P 500 closes down 1.03% at 7,340.53, its lowest close since late July, as chip stocks fall before Nvidia earnings

terms.meaning: A fall of 10% or more in a market from a recent high.
A measure that tracks the combined price of a group of shares.
A company's update on how much it sold and earned.

levels.headline: S&P 500 closes down 1.03% at 7,340.53, its lowest close since late July, as chip stocks fall before Nvidia earnings
levels.body:
The S&P 500 closed down on Tuesday, the latest completed session, falling 1.03% to 7,340.53, its lowest close since late July. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 848.75 points, or 1.64%, to finish at 50,759.42, after falling more than 1,000 points at its low. The Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.74% to 24,328.38.
CNBC linked the selling to traders dumping semiconductor shares ahead of Nvidia's much-awaited earnings report, along with a CNN report that the National Security Agency's classified communications network had gone down. Falling stocks outnumbered rising ones by nearly three to one on both the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq at midday.
It followed a bigger drop on Monday, when the S&P 500 lost 1.92% and the Nasdaq 2.49%. After the closing bell Nvidia reported results that beat expectations, its first since chief executive Jensen Huang resigned, and US stock futures edged higher. Some data providers show slightly different closing levels.
levels.why: Falling shares can hit pension funds and savings, and show how nervous investors are about technology firms.

levels.headline: US stocks fall again on Tuesday, with the S&P 500 down 1.03% to 7,340.53
levels.body:
The S&P 500, the main US share index, closed down on Tuesday, the latest completed session. It fell 1.03% to 7,340.53, its lowest finish since late July. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 848.75 points, or 1.64%, to 50,759.42, and the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.74% to 24,328.38.
Chip makers led the fall as investors sold before Nvidia's earnings report. CNBC also pointed to a CNN report that a classified National Security Agency communications network had gone down. At the lowest point the Dow was more than 1,000 points lower.
Monday had been worse, with the S&P 500 down 1.92% and the Nasdaq down 2.49%. After the market closed Nvidia reported better-than-expected results, and US stock futures rose slightly. Different data providers give slightly different closing figures.
levels.why: US market falls often spread to UK and European shares and to pensions.

levels.headline: Wall Street slides for a second day, with the S&P 500 down 1.03%
levels.body:
US shares fell for a second day on Tuesday. The S&P 500 closed down 1.03% at 7,340.53, its lowest close since late July. The Dow lost 848.75 points, or 1.64%, to end at 50,759.42, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.74% to 24,328.38.
Investors sold chip companies before the release of Nvidia's earnings, which are widely watched as a gauge of the boom in artificial intelligence. CNBC also said a report that a secret US government communications network had gone down added to the worry. At one point the Dow was down more than 1,000 points.
On Monday the S&P 500 had dropped 1.92%. Once the market closed, Nvidia posted results above expectations, the first since its boss Jensen Huang resigned, and stock futures moved higher. Data firms report slightly different closing levels.
levels.why: Swings in US tech shares affect pensions and savings in the UK too.

levels.headline: US shares fall again as investors worry before Nvidia's results
levels.body:
The main US share index, the S&P 500, fell 1.03% on Tuesday, the last full day of trading. It closed at 7,340.53, the lowest since late July. The Dow Jones index lost 848.75 points, or 1.64%, to 50,759.42. The Nasdaq, which is full of technology companies, dropped 0.74% to 24,328.38.
Investors sold shares in companies that make computer chips. They were nervous before Nvidia, a very big chip firm, published its latest sales and profit figures. A news report that a classified US communications network had stopped working also added to the worry.
Monday had been even worse, with the S&P 500 down 1.92%. After trading ended, Nvidia reported results that were better than experts expected, and share prices for the next day looked set to rise a little. Different websites show slightly different closing numbers.
levels.why: If US shares fall a lot, pensions and savings invested in them can lose value.

levels.headline: US shares fall again as investors wait for Nvidia's results
levels.body:
US shares fell for a second day on Tuesday. The S&P 500, which follows 500 big American companies, closed down 1.03% at 7,340.53, its lowest since late July. The Dow, which follows 30 large firms, lost 1.64% to 50,759.42, and the Nasdaq, full of technology firms, lost 0.74% to 24,328.38.
Investors sold shares in chip makers because they were nervous before Nvidia, a very big chip company, published its latest results. A news report that a secret US government communications network had broken down also added to the worry.
Monday had been worse, with the S&P 500 down 1.92%. After trading ended, Nvidia said it had done better than experts expected, so prices looked set to rise a little on Wednesday. Different websites give slightly different closing figures.
levels.why: Falling shares can hurt pensions and savings, and can make investors nervous.

levels.headline: US shares drop again, with the S&P 500 down 1.03%
levels.body:
US shares went down again on Tuesday. The S&P 500, a list of 500 big American companies, closed down 1.03% at 7,340.53. That is its lowest since late July. The Dow, another list of big firms, fell 1.64% to 50,759.42. The Nasdaq, full of tech companies, fell 0.74% to 24,328.38.
Many investors sold shares in chip makers before Nvidia shared its latest results. Nvidia is a huge company that makes chips used in artificial intelligence. People were also worried by a news report that a secret US government network had stopped working.
Monday had been worse, when the S&P 500 fell 1.92%. After trading closed on Tuesday, Nvidia said its results were better than people expected. Prices for Wednesday looked set to rise a little. Different sources give slightly different final numbers.
levels.why: Many pensions hold US shares, so big falls can matter to ordinary savers.

levels.headline: US shares fall for a second day, with tech firms hit hardest
levels.body:
Shares in the United States fell again on Tuesday. The S&P 500, which tracks 500 large American companies, ended the day down 1.03%. It closed at 7,340.53, its lowest level since late July. The Dow Jones, which tracks 30 big firms, lost 1.64%, and the Nasdaq, packed with tech firms, lost 0.74%.
Investors sold shares in companies that make computer chips. They were nervous ahead of results from Nvidia, a very large chip maker. They were also unsettled by a report that a secret US government communications network had broken down.
On Monday, shares had fallen even more. After trading ended on Tuesday, Nvidia said it had made more money than experts predicted. That helped prices look set to rise a little on Wednesday. Many people have savings and pensions that are partly invested in shares like these.
levels.why: Share prices affect pensions and savings, so these falls can matter to ordinary people.

levels.headline: US shares fall again as people worry about big tech firms
levels.body:
A share is a tiny piece of a company that people can buy. On Tuesday, the price of many US shares went down for the second day in a row. A list of 500 big companies, called the S&P 500, fell by 1.03%. It is now at its lowest since late July.
Another list, the Dow, fell by 1.64%. The Nasdaq list, which has many technology firms, fell by 0.74%. Lots of people sold shares in companies that make computer chips. They were nervous before a big chip company called Nvidia shared how much money it had made.
After the day's trading ended, Nvidia said it had made more money than people had guessed. That made prices look likely to go up a little on Wednesday. This matters because many people's pensions are partly invested in shares.
levels.why: Pensions are often invested in shares, so big falls can matter to families.

levels.headline: American shares go down again as people feel nervous
levels.body:
Shares are small parts of a company that people can own. On Tuesday, share prices in America went down for a second day. One big list of 500 companies, the S&P 500, fell by about 1 in every 100. That is its lowest score since the summer.
Lots of people sold shares in companies that make computer chips. A very big chip company called Nvidia was about to say how much money it had made. People felt nervous about what it might say. Some also read a worrying story about a secret government computer network.
After the day ended, Nvidia said it had done better than people expected. That is good news, so prices looked likely to rise a little on Wednesday. Prices can go up and down a lot. Many grown-ups save for retirement in shares.
levels.why: Many grown-ups save for retirement in shares, so price falls matter.

levels.headline: Share prices fell in America for a second day
levels.body:
Imagine a big market where people buy and sell tiny pieces of companies. These pieces are called shares. On Tuesday, many prices in the American market went down for the second day in a row. The main list of 500 big companies fell by about 1 in 100.
Many people sold shares in companies that make computer chips. Those chips are the tiny brains inside computers. A giant chip company called Nvidia was about to share how well it had done. People were nervous, a bit like waiting for your exam results.
After the market closed, Nvidia said it had done better than people guessed. So prices looked ready to rise a little the next day. Prices can go up and down like a seesaw. Lots of grown-ups save money for later by owning shares.
levels.why: Lots of grown-ups save for later in shares, so price drops can matter.

headline: Bank of England raises rates to 4% and warns inflation will near 5% as UK awaits October figures

terms.meaning: The price of borrowing money, set by the Bank of England as a base rate.
The rate at which prices rise over time.
Inflation leaving out volatile items such as energy and food.

levels.headline: Bank of England raises rates to 4% and warns inflation will near 5% as UK awaits October figures
levels.body:
The Bank of England raised its main interest rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 November, its first rise since the Iran war began, by eight votes to one. Catherine Mann dissented, voting for a bigger rise of half a percentage point to 4.25%.
The Bank said inflation, which was 3.5% in September, up from 3.1% in August, will rise to about 5% by the middle of 2027, mainly because of energy costs linked to the Iran war. Core inflation rose to 2.8% from 2.6%. Its forecasts put growth at 1.6% this year and 1.3% in 2027. Governor Andrew Bailey said the rise should not be seen as the first of an inevitable long sequence.
Markets were pricing in a 73% chance of another rise at the December meeting, according to LSEG data. October's inflation figure is due from the Office for National Statistics on 18 November, with a consensus forecast of 3.7%. No result was available when this was written.
levels.why: Higher rates raise mortgage and loan costs, while rising prices squeeze household budgets.

levels.headline: Bank of England lifts interest rates to 4% and warns inflation is heading towards 5%
levels.body:
The Bank of England has raised interest rates from 3.75% to 4%, its first increase since the start of the Iran war. Eight members of the Monetary Policy Committee voted for the rise and one, Catherine Mann, wanted a larger half-point increase.
The Bank expects inflation to climb to about 5% by mid-2027, up from 3.5% in September, mainly because of higher energy costs linked to the Iran war. Core inflation, which strips out volatile items, rose to 2.8%. Governor Andrew Bailey said the increase should not be seen as the start of a long run of rises.
Investors still think another rise is likely in December, with LSEG data putting the chance at 73%. The latest official inflation figure, for October, is due on 18 November. Forecasters expect 3.7%, though the actual number was not available at the time of writing.
levels.why: It decides how much people pay on mortgages and loans, and how fast prices rise.

levels.headline: Bank of England raises interest rates to 4% as it warns inflation will rise towards 5%
levels.body:
The Bank of England raised its key interest rate to 4% from 3.75% on 5 November, the first rise since the Iran war began. The vote was eight to one, with Catherine Mann favouring a bigger rise to 4.25%.
The Bank warned that inflation, currently 3.5%, will climb to about 5% by the middle of next year, with energy prices tied to the Iran war the main cause. It expects the economy to grow 1.6% this year and 1.3% in 2027. Governor Andrew Bailey said the rise should not be seen as the first in a long series.
Markets think a further rise in December is likely, with a 73% chance priced in. The Office for National Statistics publishes October's inflation figure on 18 November. The consensus is for 3.7%, but the number was not available when this was written.
levels.why: Borrowers could pay more, while savers could earn more.

levels.headline: Bank of England puts up interest rates to 4% and says prices will keep rising
levels.body:
The Bank of England has put up its main interest rate from 3.75% to 4%. This is the first increase since the war involving Iran began. Eight of nine decision-makers backed the rise, and one wanted a bigger one.
The Bank says inflation, the speed at which prices go up, will reach about 5% by the middle of next year. It was 3.5% in September. The main reason is the cost of energy, which has gone up because of the war. The Bank's boss, Andrew Bailey, said this should not be seen as the start of lots of rises in a row.
Investors think another rise in December is likely. The next official inflation figure, for October, is due on 18 November. Experts expect 3.7%, but the real number had not been published when this was written.
levels.why: Mortgage and loan payments could go up, while prices in shops keep rising.

levels.headline: Bank of England raises the cost of borrowing and warns prices will rise faster
levels.body:
The Bank of England has raised its interest rate from 3.75% to 4%. The interest rate is the price of borrowing money, and it affects mortgages, loans and savings. It is the first rise since the war involving Iran began.
The Bank thinks inflation will rise to about 5% by the middle of next year. Inflation means prices going up. It was 3.5% in September. This is mostly because energy costs more because of the war. The Bank's boss, Andrew Bailey, said this does not mean many more rises are certain.
Investors think there is a good chance of another rise in December. The next official inflation figure is due on 18 November, and experts expect 3.7%. That number had not been published when this was written.
levels.why: People with mortgages or loans may pay more, while savers may earn more.

levels.headline: The Bank of England raises interest rates because prices are going up
levels.body:
The Bank of England has raised the interest rate to 4%, up from 3.75%. The interest rate is the cost of borrowing money. When it goes up, mortgages and loans usually cost more, and savings accounts often pay more. This is the first rise since the war involving Iran started.
The Bank did it because prices are rising quickly. In September, prices were 3.5% higher than a year earlier. The Bank thinks that could reach about 5% by the middle of next year. Energy costs more because of the war, and that pushes up the price of many things.
The Bank's boss said this is not the start of lots of rises. But investors think another one in December is quite likely. New price figures for October come out on 18 November, and experts expect 3.7%.
levels.why: It affects mortgage bills, savings and how much shopping costs.

levels.headline: The Bank of England raised interest rates to try to slow rising prices
levels.body:
The Bank of England has raised its interest rate to 4%. This is the price of borrowing money. It was 3.75% before. The Bank is meant to keep prices from going up too fast. At the moment they are rising faster than it would like.
Prices are going up because energy costs more after a war involving Iran. The Bank thinks that figure could grow to about 5% by the middle of next year. This is called inflation.
Higher interest rates make borrowing cost more, so people tend to spend less, and that helps slow price rises. The Bank's boss said more rises are not certain. New figures on prices are due on 18 November. Experts expect them to be about 3.7%.
levels.why: It could make mortgages cost more but help stop prices rising too fast.

levels.headline: The Bank of England makes borrowing cost more to slow rising prices
levels.body:
The Bank of England is in charge of keeping prices steady in Britain. It has made borrowing money more expensive. It raised the interest rate to 4%. Interest is the extra money you pay back when you borrow. The rate was 3.75% before.
The Bank did this because prices are going up fast. This is called inflation. In September, prices were 3.5% higher than a year before. The Bank thinks they could go up by nearly 5% by next summer. Energy, like petrol and gas, costs more because of a war.
When borrowing costs more, people spend less. That helps stop prices rising so fast. But it also means people with a mortgage might pay more each month. The Bank's boss says it might not keep raising the rate. New price numbers come out on 18 November.
levels.why: Families with a mortgage could pay more each month.

levels.headline: The Bank of England makes borrowing cost more because prices are rising
levels.body:
Prices in shops are going up fast. When that happens, a bank called the Bank of England can step in. It has made borrowing money more expensive. It does this by raising something called the interest rate. This is the extra money you pay when you borrow.
Prices are going up because things like petrol and gas cost more. A war involving Iran is one reason. The Bank thinks prices will go up even faster by next summer. When borrowing costs more, people buy less, and that makes prices rise more slowly.
This can be hard for grown-ups who borrowed money to buy a house. They may have to pay more each month. The Bank's boss says it may not keep doing this. New numbers about prices come out on 18 November. We will see then how fast prices are rising.
levels.why: Grown-ups with home loans may pay more each month.

levels.headline: The Bank of England makes borrowing more expensive
levels.body:
Imagine you borrow some pocket money from a friend. You promise to pay back a little extra as a thank-you. That extra is called interest. The Bank of England sets how much extra people should pay when they borrow. It has just raised the amount a little.
It did this because prices in shops are going up fast. Things like petrol and gas cost more, partly because of a war far away. If people borrow less and spend less, prices rise more slowly. That is what the Bank hopes will happen.
It can be tricky for families who borrowed money to buy a home. They may have to pay a bit more each month. The Bank's boss says it may not do this again and again. Everyone will hear new news about prices on 18 November.
levels.why: Families who borrowed money for a home may pay a bit more each month.

headline: UK unemployment rate falls to 4.6% in the three months to September, ONS says

terms.meaning: The share of people who want and are looking for work but do not have a job.
People who are not working and not looking for work, such as students or long-term sick.
The share of working-age people who have a job.

levels.headline: UK unemployment rate falls to 4.6% in the three months to September, ONS says
levels.body:
The Office for National Statistics reported on 17 November that the UK unemployment rate fell to 4.6% in the three months from July to September 2026, with about 1.68 million people unemployed. The employment rate for people aged 16 to 64 was 75.4%.
The economic inactivity rate, which counts people who are neither working nor looking for work, edged down by 0.1 percentage points on the year and the quarter to 20.8%. The ONS also gave a separate ILO measure for people aged 16 to 64 of 4.8%, with the male rate of 5.0% higher than the female rate of 4.2%.
The figures come as the Bank of England weighs further interest rate rises to fight inflation. Earlier in the year unemployment had reached a five-year high, so the fall is a welcome change. The next labour market release is due on 15 December 2026.
levels.why: Jobs figures influence interest rate decisions and show how secure work feels.

levels.headline: UK unemployment falls to 4.6% as more people are in work
levels.body:
The Office for National Statistics said on 17 November that unemployment in the UK fell to 4.6% in the three months to September. That is around 1.68 million people. The employment rate among 16 to 64-year-olds stood at 75.4%.
The inactivity rate, covering people who are not working or looking for work, dipped by 0.1 percentage points to 20.8%. A different measure for those aged 16 to 64 puts unemployment at 4.8%, with the rate for men, 5.0%, above the rate for women, 4.2%.
The figures matter for the Bank of England, which has just raised interest rates and may do so again. Unemployment had hit a five-year high earlier this year, so the fall will be welcomed. The ONS will publish the next set of figures on 15 December.
levels.why: A stronger jobs market can support wages but may keep interest rates higher.

levels.headline: UK unemployment falls to 4.6% in latest official figures
levels.body:
The unemployment rate in the UK has fallen to 4.6% for the three months from July to September, the Office for National Statistics reported on 17 November. About 1.68 million people were out of work and looking for a job. The employment rate for those aged 16 to 64 was 75.4%.
The share of people who are economically inactive, meaning neither working nor looking for work, fell slightly to 20.8%. Another measure, for people aged 16 to 64, showed unemployment of 4.8%, higher for men at 5.0% than for women at 4.2%.
The Bank of England, which has recently raised interest rates, watches these figures closely. Unemployment earlier this year reached a five-year high, so the drop is a welcome sign. The next release is on 15 December 2026.
levels.why: It shows how secure jobs are and helps shape interest rate decisions.

levels.headline: Fewer people are out of work in the UK, official figures show
levels.body:
The number of people out of work in the UK has fallen. The Office for National Statistics said on 17 November that the unemployment rate dropped to 4.6% in the three months to the end of September. That means about 1.68 million people wanted a job but did not have one. Some 75.4% of people aged 16 to 64 were in work.
A further 20.8% of people were economically inactive. That means they were not working and not looking for work, for example because they were studying or too ill. That share fell slightly. A slightly different measure gave an unemployment rate of 4.8%, higher for men than for women.
The Bank of England is watching jobs closely as it decides on interest rates. Earlier this year unemployment reached a five-year high, so this is good news. New figures come out on 15 December.
levels.why: Having a job affects how much people can spend, and it influences interest rates.

headline: Ukraine says drone strikes destroyed part of the Kerch Bridge as Russia convenes emergency commission

terms.meaning: The bridge linking Crimea with mainland Russia, a key supply route for Russian forces.
An aircraft flown without a pilot on board, often controlled remotely.
Ukraine's security service.

levels.headline: Ukraine says drone strikes destroyed part of the Kerch Bridge as Russia convenes emergency commission
levels.body:
Ukrainian drones struck the Kerch Bridge linking Crimea to Russia for a second night running, closing it to traffic. Ukraine's security service, the SBU, said one of the bridge's arches and a section of the road were destroyed. Social media images appeared to show a section collapsed into the water, which CNBC could not independently verify.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called it an unprecedented operation prepared over several weeks. Russia said a government commission, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin, will meet to deal with the consequences. The Institute for the Study of War said the strikes appear to be part of Kyiv's campaign to deny Russian forces major supply routes through Crimea.
The attack came as Ukrainian, US and European negotiators held their first talks on future peace negotiations with Russia, with Jared Kushner saying progress was being made. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said a link to an upcoming Trump, Xi and Putin meeting could not be ruled out.
levels.why: The bridge is a symbol and a supply route, so damage to it could change the course of the war.

levels.headline: Ukrainian drones hit the Kerch Bridge again, closing the Crimea crossing
levels.body:
Ukrainian drones hit the Kerch Bridge, which links Crimea to Russia, for a second night in a row, and traffic across it has stopped. The SBU, Ukraine's security service, said an arch and part of the road were destroyed. Images online appeared to show a collapsed section, though CNBC could not confirm them.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy called it an unprecedented operation several weeks in the making. Russia said a government commission led by Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin would meet to handle the consequences. Analysts at the Institute for the Study of War see it as part of an effort to cut Russian forces' supply lines through Crimea.
Separately, Ukrainian, US and European negotiators held first talks about future peace negotiations, and Jared Kushner said progress was being made. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov did not rule out a link to an upcoming Trump, Xi and Putin meeting.
levels.why: The strike could hit Russian supplies and shape any peace talks.

levels.headline: Ukraine hits Crimea bridge for a second night, Russia holds emergency meeting
levels.body:
Ukrainian drones attacked the Kerch Bridge, which connects Crimea with Russia, for the second night running. The crossing is closed to traffic. Ukraine's security service says an arch and a stretch of road were destroyed, and online images appeared to show a section fallen into the water. CNBC could not verify them.
President Zelenskyy described an unprecedented operation prepared over several weeks. Russia's government said a commission chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin will meet about the consequences. Analysts at the Institute for the Study of War say the attacks fit a Ukrainian effort to deny Russia's army key supply routes through Crimea.
The strike came as Ukrainian, US and European negotiators held their first talks on future peace negotiations with Russia. Jared Kushner said progress was being made. The Kremlin said a link to an upcoming Trump, Xi and Putin meeting could not be ruled out.
levels.why: It could limit Russian supplies and affect how the war and any peace talks develop.

levels.headline: Ukraine says it has badly damaged a key bridge linking Crimea and Russia
levels.body:
Ukraine says its drones have badly damaged the Kerch Bridge, the long crossing between Crimea and Russia. It was hit for a second night in a row, and traffic has stopped. Ukraine's security service says an arch and part of the road were destroyed. Pictures online seem to show part of the bridge in the water, but CNBC could not check them.
President Zelenskyy said the attack had been planned for several weeks. Russia has set up a government group, led by Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin, to deal with the damage. Experts think Ukraine wants to cut the routes Russian forces use to bring supplies through Crimea.
At the same time, Ukrainian, US and European officials held their first talks about starting peace negotiations with Russia. US envoy Jared Kushner said progress was being made. Russia's government said it could not rule out a link to a coming meeting of Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.
levels.why: The bridge matters to Russian supplies, and the attack may affect peace talks.

levels.headline: Ukraine hits the bridge between Crimea and Russia for a second night
levels.body:
Ukraine has used drones, which are aircraft with no pilot on board, to hit the Kerch Bridge two nights in a row. The bridge joins Crimea, a region Russia took from Ukraine, to Russia itself. It is now closed to traffic. Ukraine's security service says part of the bridge and road was destroyed, though CNBC could not check pictures online.
President Zelenskyy said the plan took several weeks to prepare. Russia has called a government group, led by Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin, to deal with the damage. Experts think Ukraine wants to make it harder for Russia to bring supplies to its soldiers.
At the same time, officials from Ukraine, the United States and Europe held their first talks about starting peace negotiations. An American envoy said progress was being made. Russia said the attack might be linked to a coming meeting of three world leaders.
levels.why: The bridge helps supply Russian forces, so damage could affect the war and peace talks.

levels.headline: Ukraine hits an important bridge linking Crimea to Russia
levels.body:
Ukraine says it has damaged a very important bridge. The Kerch Bridge links Crimea, a region Russia took from Ukraine, with Russia itself. Ukrainian drones, which are aircraft with no pilot on board, hit it two nights in a row. The bridge is now closed to traffic.
Ukraine's security service says part of the bridge and the road were destroyed. President Zelenskyy said the plan took weeks to prepare. Russia has set up a government group to deal with the damage. Experts say Ukraine wants to make it harder for Russia to bring supplies to its soldiers.
At the same time, officials from Ukraine, the United States and Europe held their first talks about starting peace negotiations. A US envoy said progress was being made. Russia's government said the attack might be linked to a coming meeting of the Russian, US and Chinese leaders.
levels.why: The bridge helps Russia supply its forces, so damage could change the war.

levels.headline: Ukraine damages the bridge between Crimea and Russia
levels.body:
Ukraine has attacked a famous bridge that joins Crimea to Russia. Crimea is a region that Russia took from Ukraine. Ukraine used drones, which are flying machines with no pilot. They hit the bridge two nights in a row. Now cars and lorries cannot cross it.
Ukraine says that part of the bridge and the road fell down. Russia has called a special meeting of government officials to deal with it. Experts say the bridge is very useful to Russia because soldiers and supplies cross it. Cutting it could make the fighting harder for Russia.
At the same time, people from Ukraine, the United States and Europe met to talk about how peace talks with Russia could start. An American envoy said they were making progress. Russia says the attack might be linked to a coming meeting of three world leaders.
levels.why: A damaged bridge could make it harder for Russia to supply its soldiers.

levels.headline: Ukraine hits a big bridge that Russia uses
levels.body:
There is a war between Russia and Ukraine. Russia took a region called Crimea from Ukraine. A long bridge joins Crimea to Russia. Ukraine used drones, which are flying machines with no pilot, to hit the bridge two nights in a row. The bridge is now closed.
Ukraine says part of the bridge fell down. The bridge matters because Russia uses it to carry soldiers and supplies. If it cannot be used, it is harder for Russia to bring things to Crimea. Russia has called a special meeting to deal with the damage.
At the same time, people from Ukraine, America and Europe met to talk about ways to start peace talks. An American envoy said they were making progress. People hope the war can end, but it has not yet.
levels.why: A broken bridge could make it harder for Russia to fight.

levels.headline: Ukraine breaks part of a big bridge that Russia uses
levels.body:
Two countries, Russia and Ukraine, have been fighting for a long time. Russia took a place called Crimea from Ukraine. A very long bridge links Crimea to Russia. Ukraine sent flying machines called drones, with no pilot inside, to hit the bridge. They did it two nights in a row.
Ukraine says part of the bridge and road fell down. Nobody can drive across it now. This matters because Russia uses the bridge to send soldiers and supplies. If the bridge is broken, it is harder for Russia to get things there. Russia is holding a special meeting about it.
At the same time, some leaders met to talk about how to begin peace talks to end the war. They said they were making progress. Everyone hopes the fighting will stop one day, but that has not happened yet.
levels.why: A broken bridge could slow down Russia's army.

levels.headline: Ukraine hits a bridge that Russia needs

Imagine two groups arguing over a playground. One group, Russia, has taken a part of it, called Crimea. A long bridge is the only road from Russia to that part. Ukraine used little flying machines called drones to hit the bridge two nights in a row. Now it is closed.
Ukraine says part of the bridge fell down. This matters because Russia uses the bridge to bring food, fuel and soldiers to Crimea. Without it, that is much harder. Russia has called a special meeting to work out what to do.
At the same time, some grown-ups from Ukraine, America and Europe met to talk about starting peace talks. They said they were making progress. Everyone hopes the fighting will stop soon, but it has not yet.
levels.why: Everyone hopes the fighting ends soon, and talks have just begun.

headline: Qatar warns Gulf escalation is a 'grave danger' to US-Iran deal as Iran targets US radar in Bahrain

terms.meaning: A narrow sea route from the Gulf through which a large share of the world's oil passes.
A person or country that helps two sides in a dispute to reach agreement.
Stopping ships from entering or leaving a place.

levels.headline: Qatar warns Gulf escalation is a 'grave danger' to US-Iran deal as Iran targets US radar in Bahrain
levels.body:
Qatar warned on Tuesday that escalation in the Gulf poses a grave danger to the chances of a deal between the US and Iran, and announced a meeting with Iranian officials later that day. Its spokesman said talks would focus on proposals already under discussion.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they launched drones at a US radar system at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Airbase. Bahrain, home to the US Navy's Fifth Fleet, and US Central Command said the drones were intercepted without damage. The US retaliated with strikes on a missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island. Donald Trump has said he will keep the naval blockade on Iran, while Tehran continues to disrupt shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran has put forward a two-day proposal via Qatari mediators demanding the lifting of sanctions and a new shipping route in the Strait of Hormuz. Mr Trump earlier said the war could end fairly soon, but kept open the option of new strikes.
levels.why: The war affects oil and energy prices, which feed through to UK bills and inflation.

levels.headline: Qatar warns of 'grave danger' as Iran fires drones at US base in Bahrain
levels.body:
Qatar has warned that escalation in the Gulf is a grave danger to hopes of a US-Iran deal, and announced new talks with Iranian officials on Tuesday. The talks are expected to cover proposals already on the table.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they launched drones at a US radar system at Sheikh Isa Airbase in Bahrain, where the US Navy's Fifth Fleet is based. Bahrain and US Central Command said they intercepted the drones, with no damage. The US responded by striking a missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island, and says its naval blockade of Iran will stay.
Iran has offered a two-day proposal through Qatar, asking for sanctions to be lifted and a new shipping route in the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump says the war could end fairly soon, but has not ruled out more strikes.
levels.why: Energy prices and inflation in the UK depend on whether the war ends.

levels.headline: Qatar says Gulf escalation threatens US-Iran deal after drone attack on Bahrain base
levels.body:
Qatar said on Tuesday that rising tension in the Gulf is a grave danger to efforts to reach a deal between the US and Iran. It announced new talks with Iranian officials later that day, to look at proposals already being discussed.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they had launched drones at a US radar system at an air base in Bahrain, home of the US Navy's Fifth Fleet. Bahrain and US Central Command said the drones were intercepted without damage. The US hit a missile launch site on Qeshm Island in response. President Trump says the naval blockade of Iran will continue, and Iran is still disrupting shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran has asked via Qatar for sanctions to be lifted and for a new shipping route in the Strait. Mr Trump has said the war could end fairly soon but left new strikes open.
levels.why: The conflict influences oil prices and therefore the cost of living.

levels.headline: Qatar says fighting in the Gulf could ruin hopes of a deal between the US and Iran
levels.body:
Qatar, which is helping the US and Iran to talk to each other, said on Tuesday that rising fighting in the Gulf is a grave danger to a deal. It said it would meet Iranian officials later that day to discuss ideas already on the table.
Iran said it had sent drones to attack a US radar at an air base in Bahrain, where the US Navy has a major fleet. Bahrain and the US military said they stopped the drones and that no damage was done. The US then struck a missile site on an Iranian island. President Trump says the US will keep its naval blockade of Iran.
Iran has asked, through Qatar, for sanctions to be lifted and for a new shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for oil. Mr Trump says the war could end fairly soon, but has not ruled out new strikes.
levels.why: The war has pushed up energy prices, which affects bills and prices at home.

levels.headline: Qatar warns that fighting near Iran could stop peace talks
levels.body:
Qatar is trying to help the US and Iran reach a deal to end their war. On Tuesday it warned that more fighting in the Gulf could ruin the chances of success. It said it would meet Iranian officials again that day.
Iran said it had flown drones at a US radar at an air base in Bahrain. The US and Bahrain said they shot the drones down, and nothing was damaged. The US then hit a missile site on an Iranian island. The US is also stopping ships from reaching Iran, which is called a blockade.
Iran has asked, through Qatar, for the US to end sanctions on it and for a new shipping route through a narrow stretch of sea called the Strait of Hormuz. A lot of the world's oil travels there. President Trump says the war could end fairly soon but might not.
levels.why: The war affects the price of oil, which affects petrol and heating bills.

levels.headline: Qatar says more fighting could spoil talks to end the US-Iran war
levels.body:
The United States and Iran are at war. Qatar, a small rich country in the Gulf, is acting as a go-between to try to end it. On Tuesday, Qatar said more fighting could ruin the chances of a deal. It also said it would meet Iranian officials again that day.
Iran said it had sent drones to attack a US radar at a base in Bahrain. The US and Bahrain said they stopped the drones, and nothing was damaged. The US hit back by bombing a missile site on an Iranian island. America is also stopping ships from getting to Iran.
Iran wants the US to lift its sanctions, which are rules that stop others trading with it. It also wants a new shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, where much of the world's oil passes. President Trump says the war could end soon, but he has not promised.
levels.why: The war has made oil and gas cost more, so it affects bills.

levels.headline: Qatar says more fighting could stop talks to end the war with Iran

America and Iran are at war. A country called Qatar is trying to help them make peace. On Tuesday, Qatar said more fighting could ruin the chances. It said it would meet people from Iran again that day to talk about ideas that are already on the table.
Iran said it sent flying machines called drones to hit a US radar at a base in Bahrain. The US and Bahrain said they stopped them, and nothing was broken. Then the US hit a place in Iran where missiles are launched. America is also keeping ships from reaching Iran.
Iran wants America to stop its sanctions, which are rules that stop people trading with Iran. It also wants a new sea route for ships. Much of the world's oil goes by ship through that area. The US President says the war could end soon, but he is not sure.
levels.why: The war makes oil cost more, so petrol and heating can cost more.

levels.headline: Qatar asks America and Iran to calm down and talk

America and Iran are fighting a war. A country called Qatar is trying to help them stop. On Tuesday, Qatar said more fighting could make peace harder. It said it would meet people from Iran again that day to talk.
Iran said it sent drones, which are flying machines without pilots, to hit a US base in Bahrain. The US and Bahrain said they stopped them. Nothing was damaged. Then America hit a place in Iran where missiles are launched. America is also stopping ships from reaching Iran.
Iran wants America to end its rules that stop people trading with Iran. It also wants a new sea road for ships. A lot of the world's oil goes through that area. When ships are stopped, oil can cost more. The US President says the war could end fairly soon, but he is not sure.
levels.why: The war can make petrol and heating cost more.

levels.headline: A small country asks America and Iran to talk instead of fight

America and Iran are fighting a war. A small country called Qatar is trying to help them stop. It is like a friend who steps in when two people are arguing. On Tuesday, Qatar said more fighting makes peace harder to reach. It said it would talk to Iran again that day.
Iran said it sent drones, which are flying machines without pilots, towards an American base in another country, Bahrain. The base stopped them, and nobody was hurt. Then America hit a place in Iran where missiles are launched. America is also stopping ships from going to Iran.
Iran wants America to stop its rules about trading. It also wants a new sea road for ships, because a lot of the world's oil goes by ship. When ships are stopped, oil costs more, and so do petrol and heating. The President says the war may end fairly soon.
levels.why: When oil costs more, petrol and heating cost more too.

levels.headline: A small country tries to help two big countries stop fighting
levels.body:
Imagine two big kids in the playground who are fighting. A smaller kid, called Qatar, steps in to help them stop. America and Iran are the two big countries. They are in a real war. On Tuesday, Qatar said more fighting could make it harder to make peace. It will talk to Iran again.
Iran said it flew little pilotless planes called drones at an American base. The base stopped them, and nothing was broken. Then America hit back at a place in Iran. America is also blocking ships from reaching Iran, like a gate across a road.
Iran wants the gate opened and some rules lifted. Lots of the world's oil goes on ships through that area. When ships cannot move freely, oil costs more, and so do petrol and heating. The American President says the war may end fairly soon.
levels.why: Oil and petrol can cost more while the fighting goes on.

headline: Brent crude slips to about $91.80 a barrel, down around 16% in a month but still 41% above a year ago

terms.meaning: The main international benchmark price for oil, quoted in dollars per barrel.
The standard unit for oil, about 159 litres.
When more oil is produced than buyers need, which tends to push prices down.

levels.headline: Brent crude slips to about $91.80 a barrel, down around 16% in a month but still 41% above a year ago
levels.body:
Brent crude, the international oil benchmark, stood at $91.80 a barrel on 17 November, down 0.7% on the previous day, according to Trading Economics. The price has fallen about 16% over the past month but remains around 41% higher than a year earlier. US crude was near $85.70 a barrel.
Analysts point to a supply surplus, with the International Energy Agency expecting the global oil market to return to surplus in the fourth quarter. CNBC reported on 18 November that prices fell again as higher US crude stocks eased supply worries.
Prices are still being influenced by the US-Iran war, with Tehran disrupting shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the US keeping a naval blockade on Iran. Oil costs feed into petrol prices, heating bills and inflation, which the Bank of England expects to near 5% by mid-2027.
levels.why: Oil prices affect fuel, transport and energy bills, and so the pace of inflation.

levels.headline: Oil prices keep falling as supply worries ease, but Brent is still about $92 a barrel
levels.body:
Brent crude, the global benchmark, was $91.80 a barrel on 17 November, down 0.7% on the day, according to Trading Economics. That is about 16% lower than a month ago but still about 41% higher than a year ago. US crude was around $85.70.
Analysts say a supply surplus is building, with the International Energy Agency expecting the market to move into surplus in the fourth quarter. CNBC said oil fell again on 18 November after higher US crude stocks eased worries about supply.
The war between the US and Iran still matters, as Iran is disrupting shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the US is blockading Iran. Oil prices help determine petrol costs, energy bills and inflation, which the Bank of England expects to near 5% by the middle of 2027.
levels.why: Lower oil prices could help ease pressure on bills and inflation.

levels.headline: Oil falls again as supply surplus looms, with Brent near $92

Oil prices have fallen again. Brent crude, the main international benchmark, was $91.80 a barrel on 17 November, down 0.7% in a day, according to Trading Economics. It is about 16% lower over a month but still about 41% above where it was a year ago.
The International Energy Agency expects the global oil market to swing back into surplus in the fourth quarter, meaning more oil is available than buyers need. CNBC reported that on 18 November, higher US crude stocks reduced concerns about supply.
The conflict between the US and Iran continues to affect the market, because Iran is disrupting shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the US is blockading Iranian ports. Oil prices influence petrol and energy bills as well as inflation, which the Bank of England expects to near 5% by mid-2027.
levels.why: Oil prices feed into petrol, bills and inflation.

levels.headline: Oil prices fall again, but are still much higher than last year
levels.body:
The price of oil has gone down again. Brent crude, the price used around the world, was $91.80 a barrel on 17 November. A barrel is a large container of oil. That is about 16% less than a month ago, but about 41% more than a year ago.
Experts say there may soon be more oil than people want to buy. That usually pushes prices down. A report on 18 November said US oil stores had grown, which also eased worries about supply.
The war involving Iran still matters, because ships have trouble sailing through a key route called the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices affect petrol, heating bills and the cost of moving goods. The Bank of England expects prices overall to rise towards 5% a year by the middle of next year.
levels.why: Oil prices help decide petrol prices, heating bills and the cost of living.

levels.headline: Oil prices fall again, but are still far higher than a year ago
levels.body:
The price of oil has fallen again. The main world price, called Brent, was $91.80 for a barrel, a big drum of oil, on 17 November. That is about 16% cheaper than a month ago. But it is still about 41% dearer than a year ago.
Experts expect there may soon be more oil than buyers need. When that happens, prices tend to drop. A report on 18 November also said US oil stores had grown, which eased worries about running short.
A war involving Iran still matters, because it has disrupted ships on an important sea route. Oil is used to make petrol and to move goods about. When oil costs more, petrol, heating and many things in the shops can cost more too.
levels.why: Oil prices affect petrol, heating bills and shop prices.

levels.headline: Oil gets cheaper again but costs much more than a year ago

levels.why: Oil prices affect petrol, bills and prices in shops.

levels.headline: The price of oil is falling, but it is still high

But it is still much higher than a year ago, by about 41%. Experts think there may soon be more oil than people want to buy. This pushes prices down, like fruit that is cheaper when there is lots of it.
The war involving Iran still matters. Ships have had trouble using a very important sea route. When oil costs more, things like petrol, bus fares and heating can cost more as well. That is one reason prices in shops have been going up.

levels.headline: Oil is getting cheaper, but not as cheap as last year
